acceptance: Unit tests under a tmp lock dir prove: (a) contended acquire with WAIT_SECONDS=0 exits non-zero naming holder pid, command and live waiter count; (b) after `kill -9` of the holder a waiter acquires within 2 s; (c) a descendant with the owner env skips acquisition; (d) an unrelated process given a copied owner env does not skip; (e) owner env with a wrong create_time is rejected; (f) nested acquire in the same process does not block and the lock is released only after the outer release; (g) a waiter whose fd points at an unlinked inode never reports itself as holder; (h) a descendant with the owner env scrubbed fails immediately (< 2 s) with an env-scrub message instead of waiting.

`python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run -- sleep 5` holds the lock (a parallel WAIT_SECONDS=0 acquire is refused) and releases it on exit; SIGTERM and SIGINT to the wrapper each stop the child and release the lock; a child that reads stdin under `make` does not hang; `make test-unlock` clears only an inactive lock.
`git grep -n local_validation` shows no lock-helper callers; `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py` has no private flock/msvcrt code.
Path-filter, ledger and cutover drift tests pass with host_lock included (`tests/unit/scripts/test_path_filter_decision.py`, `tests/unit/test_ledger_coverage.py`).
Existing `tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py` and data_fetch locking tests pass without weakened assertions.
G1 import-time numbers recorded in the PR body.
`make comment-policy-check`, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make duplicate-check-delta`, `make test-fast` pass; PR CI green including the Windows framing job.

description:
## Problem
The host lock that serializes heavy work lives in `scripts/local_validation.py` and is loaded by file path from `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/utilities/session_isolation.py` and `_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py`. Product code cannot reuse it. Defects: a process that already holds the lock deadlocks if it asks again (a second flock on a new fd returns EWOULDBLOCK); the inheritance check trusts a bare PID (PID reuse); a lock file unlinked and recreated lets a second holder run (`~/.benchbox/test.lock.stale-20260831-1504` shows replacement happened); a child whose environment was scrubbed waits up to an hour on its own ancestor. A second flock helper exists in `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py`.

## Change
1. New module `benchbox/utils/host_lock.py` owning all host-lock logic: flock/msvcrt primitives, holder record, wait loop, clear-inactive, ownership check. Move `seek_lock_byte`, `read_holder`, `write_holder`, `_close_lock`, `wait_on_fd`, `wait_for_lock`, `clear_inactive_lock` out of `scripts/local_validation.py`; migrate every caller (conftest, session_isolation, `_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py`, Makefile `test-unlock`, `tests/integration/worktree/test_pr_process.py:29`, `tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py:13`) and delete the old copies.
2. Point `benchbox/core/data_fetch/locking.py` at the same primitives (one flock/msvcrt implementation).
3. Lock path: `<real home>/.benchbox/test.lock`, real home from `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir` on POSIX, `Path.home()` on Windows; `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` still overrides the directory.
4. After every successful flock, compare `fstat(fd).st_ino` with `stat(path).st_ino`; on mismatch close and retry. Expose `held_inode_matches()`.
5. Ownership: holder record and `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` carry `<pid>:<create_time>` (`psutil.Process.create_time()`; psutil is a hard dependency, pyproject.toml:31). Skip acquisition only if the owner is the current process or an ancestor, create_time matches, the holder record names that owner, and the lock is held. Same-process re-entry returns the existing handle with a reference count. If the holder record names an ancestor of the waiter but the owner env is missing or mismatched, fail immediately with a message naming the env scrub; never wait on an ancestor.
6. Waiters register `<lockdir>/test.lock.waiters/<pid>`; the blocked message shows the count of live waiters.
7. CLI: `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run -- <cmd>` (holds for the child's lifetime, exports owner env, the wrapper forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP to the child's process group; the child keeps the terminal foreground, or stdin is redirected from /dev/null when the wrapper is not in the foreground, so it never stops on SIGTTIN), `clear` (replaces `scripts/local_validation.py clear-test-lock`).
8. Drift guards the move touches: add `benchbox/utils/host_lock.py` to `.github/path-filters.yml` framing filter and `FRAMING_TRIGGER_PATHS`; extend the first-party walk in `tests/unit/scripts/test_path_filter_decision.py` (:207) to `benchbox.utils.host_lock`; update `docs/internal/dev-loop-property-ledger.md` (:250, :379) and `tests/unit/ledger_cutover_files.txt` (:83). Windows msvcrt tests stay in the framing job; POSIX-only tests (`kill -9`, `fcntl`) skip on win32.

## Decision gates
- D1 (resolved): keep existing names; renaming is out of scope.
- D2 (resolved): default wait stays 3600 s; `WAIT_SECONDS=0` fails fast. A shorter default without a TTY was considered and rejected: agents run long commands as background jobs, and a short default would turn waits into retries that race for the lock.
- G1 (stop condition): measure `python -X importtime -c 'import benchbox.utils.host_lock'`. If it pulls non-stdlib packages beyond psutil or adds >100 ms over bare interpreter start, the pytest plugin loads the module by file path; in that case the module may not import other `benchbox` modules and uses `time.monotonic` through a single local helper, recorded in the PR. Record numbers either way.
- Known limit (record in docs on heavy-guard-status-policy): `kill -9` of the `run` wrapper leaves its child running unlocked; fork-without-exec children inherit the flock.

## Guardrails (all heavy-guard items)
- Linked worktree from `origin/develop` via `make worktree-create`; never the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; never `git add -A`.
- `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`: no comments or docstrings in new code. Durations use `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`/`elapsed_seconds()`.
- Tests use `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` under `tmp_path` and injected readings; never touch the real `~/.benchbox/test.lock` or depend on live host pressure, VMs or disk.
- Never delete, move or recreate a lock file from code; never stop, resize or signal processes/VMs this invocation did not start.
- Keep names `test.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` (rename deferred on heavy-guard-status-policy).
- No automatic skip on `CI` or `BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE` (agent shells export `CI=true`).
- No heavy verification runs (no benchmark sweeps above scale 0.01, no real compose stacks) unless the item names one.

## Non-goals
Admission, watchdog, new acquirers.
